mutants.description: The cycle-boundary strobe fires on the falling edge of pwm_sync (high-side turn-off, the peak) instead of the rising edge (end of low-side conduction, the valley).
mutants.reason: Each window sample is taken at PWM falling edges, so the cp_delay value BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-off is counted. When cp_sync is high only during the low-side period (or only during the high-side period), fault_count_*_out and window_trip/window_trip_SS differ from the valley-sampled reference.

mutants.description: The blanking history cp_delay advances once per switching cycle (on pwm_rise) instead of once per clock, so the lookback is BLANK_CLKS cycles rather than BLANK_CLKS clocks.
mutants.reason: While active, the sample added at each pwm_rise is the comparator state from several switching cycles earlier, not from a few clocks before turn-on. A burst of overcurrent shows up in fault_count_*_out and the trip outputs several cycles late, and a cp_sync pulse just before one turn-on is missed.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window samples the live cp_sync at pwm_rise instead of the blanked cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1] value from before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a cp_sync that is high at the turn-on edge but was low BLANK_CLKS clocks earlier (or the other way round) is counted differently. fault_count_run_out and window_trip change, while the S_SS path is unaffected.

mutants.description: The soft-start count adds the live cp_sync while the SS shift register stores the blanked cp_delay sample, so the count and the window contents diverge.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, when cp_sync at pwm_rise differs from cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1], the count gains or loses one against the window. fault_count_ss_out drifts, and can wrap when the bit leaves 32 cycles later, so window_trip_SS asserts or fails to assert wrongly.

mutants.description: The soft-start count adds the previous cycle's sample (fault_shifter_SS[0]) as the entering bit instead of the new sample being shifted in.
mutants.reason: In S_SS the count lags the window by one switching cycle and covers only 31 cycles. After a sustained overcurrent, window_trip_SS asserts one cycle late, and it never asserts when trip_ss equals WINDOW_SS.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window is rewritten to insert the new sample at the MSB and shift right, but the count still subtracts bit WINDOW_RUN-1 as the leaving bit, which is now the newest sample.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN the count subtracts the sample added one cycle earlier instead of the one 16 cycles old. fault_count_run_out never rises above 1 during sustained overcurrent (and wraps when faults stop), so window_trip does not assert for trip_run of 2 or more.

mutants.description: The soft-start window and count are cleared on every S_RUN sample, instead of being held through S_RUN for telemetry.
mutants.reason: After the S_SS -> S_RUN transition, fault_count_ss_out drops to 0 at the first pwm_rise in S_RUN. It should keep the value reached at the end of soft start.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window is also advanced during S_SS, so it enters S_RUN pre-loaded with soft-start overcurrent history.
mutants.reason: fault_count_run_out becomes nonzero during S_SS when cp_delay is sampled high. On entry to S_RUN, window_trip can assert immediately because of faulted cycles that happened during the expected soft-start inrush.

mutants.description: The idle clear of both windows is qualified by pwm_rise like the update branches, so the windows clear only if PWM is still toggling while neither state is active.
mutants.reason: When the converter leaves S_RUN/S_SS and pwm_sync stops (or no rising edge comes before re-entry), the counts are not cleared. fault_count_*_out keep their old values in idle, and the retry starts on the old history, so the trip asserts again early.

mutants.description: The idle clear resets the two counts but leaves the two shift registers holding the faulted history from before the hiccup.
mutants.reason: After a retry, the old 1s shift out of the window and are subtracted from a count that was cleared to 0. fault_count_*_out wrap to a large value and window_trip / window_trip_SS assert without any new overcurrent.

mutants.description: window_trip is gated by 'not in soft start' instead of 'in S_RUN', so it is not suppressed in the idle states.
mutants.reason: On the clock S_RUN is left with fault_count_run at or above trip_run, the run count is cleared only at the next edge. window_trip therefore stays high for one clock outside S_RUN.

mutants.description: window_trip_SS is gated by 'converter switching' (S_SS or S_RUN) instead of S_SS only, so the frozen soft-start count can trip it during S_RUN.
mutants.reason: If fault_count_ss reached trip_ss on the edge the FSM left S_SS, or trip_ss is lowered during S_RUN below the held count, window_trip_SS is high throughout S_RUN.

mutants.description: The cycle-boundary strobe fires on both edges of pwm_sync, so the windows take two samples per switching cycle (valley and peak) instead of one at the valley.
mutants.reason: In S_SS and S_RUN, every switching cycle now moves each window and its count by two samples. A sustained overcurrent raises fault_count_*_out twice as fast, and window_trip / window_trip_SS assert after about half as many cycles.

mutants.description: The blanking history shifts toward bit 0 with cp_sync entering at the MSB, so the tapped bit cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1] holds cp_sync from one clock ago instead of from BLANK_CLKS clocks ago.
mutants.reason: Suppose cp_sync changes within the BLANK_CLKS clocks before pwm_rise, for example during the high-side turn-on slew. The sample stored in the window and added to fault_count_run_out / fault_count_ss_out then takes the new value, not the earlier one, and this can raise or block window_trip.

mutants.description: The soft-start window keeps advancing during S_RUN together with the run window, instead of being frozen at its S_SS value for telemetry.
mutants.reason: After S_SS -> S_RUN, fault_count_ss_out changes with every S_RUN sample (for example it drains to 0 when there is no overcurrent) instead of holding the count that soft start ended with.

mutants.description: The idle clear resets the run window but leaves the soft-start window and count holding the history from before the hiccup.
mutants.reason: After window_trip_SS sends the FSM to S_HICCUP, fault_count_ss_out stays at or above trip_ss. On the retry into S_SS, window_trip_SS asserts at once, so the part hiccups again without any new overcurrent.

mutants.description: The idle clear resets the soft-start window but leaves the run window and count holding the history from before the hiccup.
mutants.reason: After window_trip ends a run, fault_count_run_out keeps its tripped value through S_HICCUP and the next S_SS. On re-entry to S_RUN, window_trip asserts immediately even with no overcurrent.

mutants.description: window_trip is registered, so it follows the run count and run_active one clock late.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, window_trip rises one clock after fault_count_run_out reaches trip_run. After S_RUN is left, it stays high for one more clock even though run_active is low.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
else begin window_trip <= run_active && (pmic_types_pkg::TRIP_W'(fault_count_run) >= trip_run); end

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip compares the run count for equality with trip_run instead of 'at or above' it.
mutants.reason: If TRIP_RUN is lowered during S_RUN to below the current fault_count_run_out, window_trip does not assert even though the count exceeds the threshold. It asserts only if the count later falls back to exactly trip_run.

mutants.description: The soft-start telemetry output is gated by ss_active like window_trip_SS, so it reads 0 outside S_SS instead of reporting the held count.
mutants.reason: After a soft start with some faulted cycles, fault_count_ss_out reads 0 throughout S_RUN instead of the frozen non-zero count.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip is evaluated only on the cycle-boundary strobe pwm_rise, as if the trip were sampled with the window, instead of following the run count continuously.
mutants.reason: The run count takes its new value on the clock edge that ends the pwm_rise clock, so a count that reaches trip_run only raises window_trip at the next pwm_rise. That is a whole switching cycle late, and window_trip is then a one-clock pulse instead of a level held while the count is at or above trip_run in S_RUN.

mutants.description: A TRIP_RUN threshold of zero is treated as 'S_RUN window trip disabled' instead of 'trip at any count'.
mutants.reason: With trip_run programmed to 0, the original asserts window_trip as soon as run_active is high, because count >= 0 is always true. The mutant never asserts window_trip in S_RUN, whatever overcurrent is sampled.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip looks ahead at the sample being taken on pwm_rise, adding the entering bit without subtracting the leaving bit, instead of comparing the registered count.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, on a pwm_rise clock where the blanked sample is faulted and fault_count_ss is trip_ss-1, window_trip_SS rises one clock early. If the bit leaving the window is also faulted, the count never actually reaches trip_ss, but window_trip_SS still pulses high for that clock.
after: always_comb window_trip_SS = ss_active  && ((fault_count_ss + FCNT_SS_W'(pwm_rise & cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1])) >= trip_ss);

mutants.description: The blanking history cp_delay is not cleared while neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active, so it keeps tracking cp_sync through idle and hiccup.
mutants.reason: Suppose cp_sync is high during the last BLANK_CLKS clocks before S_SS is entered (after reset the CP synchroniser resets high, or the comparator is still asserted after a trip). If a pwm_rise then comes within BLANK_CLKS clocks of S_SS entry, the soft-start window counts a faulted cycle where the original counts a clean one. This raises fault_count_ss_out and can assert window_trip_SS early.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count is updated as 'increment on a faulted entering sample, else decrement on a faulted leaving sample', forgetting the case where a faulted sample enters while a faulted one leaves, so it increments instead of holding.
mutants.reason: Once the 16-cycle run window has filled, any faulted cycle that coincides with a faulted cycle leaving the window raises the count. For example, with an overcurrent on every other cycle in S_RUN the true count is 8, but fault_count_run_out keeps climbing and window_trip asserts at trip_run even though it should not.

mutants.description: The soft-start count tests the leaving bit before the entering bit, so a cycle where a faulted sample leaves and a faulted sample enters decrements the count instead of holding it.
mutants.reason: With a periodic overcurrent in S_SS whose period divides 32 (every other cycle, say), fault_count_ss_out falls after the window fills, wraps below zero to a large value, and falsely asserts window_trip_SS.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count subtracts the most recent stored sample (bit 0, per the 'most recent cycle in bit 0' convention) instead of the oldest sample leaving the window at bit WINDOW_RUN-1.
mutants.reason: The count telescopes to just the latest sample (0 or 1), so in S_RUN fault_count_run_out never goes above 1. A sustained overcurrent never trips window_trip for any trip_run of 2 or more.

mutants.description: Blanking is applied only to the S_RUN window: the soft-start window and its count both take the live cp_sync at pwm_rise instead of the blanked cp_delay sample.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, a comparator glitch present at the turn-on clock but absent BLANK_CLKS clocks earlier is counted as a faulted cycle, and a fault that ended inside the blanking interval is missed. This changes fault_count_ss_out and can falsely assert (or fail to assert) window_trip_SS.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip counts one faulted cycle too many when comparing with trip_run, so window_trip asserts when the window holds trip_run-1 faulted cycles.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with exactly trip_run-1 faulted cycles in the window (11 with the default 12), window_trip asserts and the supervisor goes into hiccup. The correct design would keep running.

mutants.description: window_trip_SS is suppressed only in S_RUN instead of being allowed only in S_SS, so it is not gated in the idle and hiccup states.
mutants.reason: After a soft-start trip the supervisor leaves S_SS. On the first idle clock, before the idle clear empties the window, the count is still at or above trip_ss, so window_trip_SS stays high for an extra clock outside S_SS. The same happens throughout idle if trip_ss is 0.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window takes as its sample 'cp_sync high in any of the last BLANK_CLKS clocks' (OR of the whole blanking history) instead of the one comparator value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a CP excursion that happens in the last few clocks before pwm_rise but not at the tapped clock counts as a faulted cycle. fault_count_run_out reads higher and window_trip asserts after fewer real valley overcurrent cycles.

mutants.description: A TRIP_SS threshold of zero is treated as 'soft-start window trip disabled' instead of 'trip at any count'.
mutants.reason: With trip_ss programmed to 0, window_trip_SS stays low for the whole of S_SS where it should be high from the first clock of S_SS. So the supervisor completes soft start instead of going to hiccup.

mutants.description: window_trip_SS is registered, so it follows the soft-start count and ss_active one clock late.
mutants.reason: When the soft-start count reaches trip_ss, window_trip_SS rises one clock late. It also stays high for one clock after S_SS is left, so a trip that coincides with SS_done is seen in S_RUN and logged by fault_cause, and the hiccup is entered a clock late.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.description: The soft-start trip counts one faulted cycle too many when comparing with trip_ss, so window_trip_SS asserts when the window holds trip_ss-1 faulted cycles.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, window_trip_SS asserts and the supervisor goes to hiccup one faulted switching cycle earlier than TRIP_SS specifies. With trip_ss of 1 it trips at once with no faulted cycle.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip looks ahead at the sample being taken on pwm_rise, adding the entering bit without subtracting the leaving bit, instead of comparing the registered run count.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with fault_count_run at trip_run-1, a faulted sample at pwm_rise asserts window_trip one clock early. If the oldest sample leaving the window is also faulted, it raises a one-clock spurious trip that sends the supervisor to hiccup even though the count never reaches trip_run.
after: always_comb window_trip    = run_active && (pmic_types_pkg::TRIP_W'(fault_count_run) + pmic_types_pkg::TRIP_W'(pwm_rise && cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1]) >= trip_run);

mutants.description: The soft-start count subtracts the leaving bit at the run-window depth (bit WINDOW_RUN-1) instead of the oldest bit of the 32-cycle soft-start window, so fault_count_ss covers only the last 16 cycles.
mutants.reason: When more than 16 faulted samples fall in the last 32 soft-start cycles, fault_count_ss_out stops at 16 instead of the real count. With trip_ss above 16, window_trip_SS then never asserts during S_SS, and with lower thresholds it asserts late or drops early.

mutants.description: The soft-start telemetry output reports the run count of the present state while in S_RUN, instead of the soft-start count that is held through S_RUN for telemetry.
mutants.reason: After S_SS -> S_RUN, fault_count_ss_out shows fault_count_run (0 at entry, then the run-window count) instead of the frozen soft-start count. Any soft start that saw faulted cycles shows this difference.

mutants.description: The run-count telemetry output is registered, so it follows fault_count_run one clock late instead of showing the live count.
mutants.reason: Each time a faulted run sample changes fault_count_run at pwm_rise, and each time the idle clear runs after S_RUN is left, fault_count_run_out shows the old value for one more clock. For that clock it disagrees with the count that drives window_trip.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.description: The S_RUN window records the start of an overcurrent excursion (faulted cycle following a clear one) instead of the comparator level, so a sustained fault is logged only on every other cycle.
mutants.reason: With cp_sync held high through S_RUN the run window fills 1,0,1,0..., so fault_count_run_out reaches only 8 and window_trip asserts later, or never when trip_run is above 8, where the original trips after trip_run cycles.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count adds the live cp_sync while the S_RUN shift register stores the blanked cp_delay sample, so the run count and the run window contents diverge.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, when the comparator at high-side turn-on differs from its value BLANK_CLKS clocks earlier (for example a slew glitch at pwm_rise), fault_count_run_out and window_trip change while the stored window does not, and the count later drifts or wraps when those bits leave.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count adds the previous cycle's stored sample (fault_shifter_RUN[0]) as the entering bit instead of the new blanked sample being shifted in.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN the run count lags the window by one switching cycle, so fault_count_run_out and window_trip respond one cycle late to the onset of an overcurrent and miss the first faulted cycle entirely if it is the most recent.

mutants.description: The soft-start count subtracts the most recent stored sample (bit 0) instead of the oldest sample leaving the 32-cycle window at bit WINDOW_SS-1.
mutants.reason: During S_SS a sustained overcurrent leaves fault_count_ss stuck at 1 instead of climbing, so window_trip_SS does not assert for trip_ss above 1, and an isolated faulted cycle makes the count wrap to all-ones on the following cycle.

mutants.description: The blanking history only advances while PWM is low (low-side conduction), freezing during the high side, so the tap reads BLANK_CLKS low-side clocks back instead of BLANK_CLKS clocks back.
mutants.reason: In S_SS or S_RUN at high duty cycle, when the low-side period is shorter than BLANK_CLKS clocks, the sample at pwm_rise comes from the previous cycle's low-side period instead of the comparator BLANK_CLKS clocks earlier, so faulted or clear cycles are logged differently in the counts and trips.

mutants.description: The run-count telemetry output is gated by run_active, so it reads 0 on the clock after S_RUN is left instead of reporting the run count before the idle clear.
mutants.reason: When the supervisor leaves S_RUN (to S_HICCUP or S_OFF) with a non-zero run count, the original shows that count for one clock until the idle clear, and the mutant shows 0.

mutants.description: A TRIP_RUN threshold above WINDOW_RUN is clamped to a full window instead of never being reached, so a completely faulted run window always trips.
mutants.reason: With trip_run set from 17 to 63 and 16 consecutive faulted cycles in S_RUN, the mutant asserts window_trip while the original never does.

mutants.description: A TRIP_SS threshold above WINDOW_SS is clamped to a full soft-start window instead of never being reached, so a completely faulted soft-start window always trips.
mutants.reason: With trip_ss set from 33 to 63 and 32 consecutive faulted cycles in S_SS, the mutant asserts window_trip_SS while the original never does.

mutants.description: The 5-bit run count is widened to the 6-bit threshold width by putting the pad bit on the wrong (LSB) side, so the S_RUN trip compares twice the faulted-cycle count with trip_run.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with trip_run = N, window_trip asserts once the run window holds ceil(N/2) faulted cycles instead of N, e.g. at 4 faulted cycles for trip_run = 8.

mutants.description: The entering sample is replicated across the run-count width instead of zero-extended, so a faulted cycle entering the S_RUN window adds all-ones (-1) to the count instead of +1.
mutants.reason: On the first faulted valley sample in S_RUN, fault_count_run_out wraps from 0 to 31 instead of rising to 1, and window_trip asserts for any trip_run up to 31.

mutants.description: The bit leaving the soft-start window is replicated across the count width instead of zero-extended, so a faulted cycle leaving the 32-cycle window adds one to fault_count_ss instead of subtracting one.
mutants.reason: In a soft start longer than 32 cycles, once a faulted sample ages out of the window fault_count_ss_out rises by 1 (rather than falling by 1), so the count overstates the window and window_trip_SS can assert with fewer than trip_ss faulted cycles present.

mutants.description: The new soft-start sample is replicated across the whole window register instead of being zero-extended into bit 0, so one faulted cycle marks every slot of the soft-start window as faulted.
mutants.reason: After one faulted valley sample in S_SS, the next sample sees a faulted bit leaving at WINDOW_SS-1 and decrements fault_count_ss (wrapping to 63 from 0), so fault_count_ss_out and window_trip_SS go wrong from the next cycle on.

mutants.description: The soft-start window counts a cycle as faulted only if the comparator was high on every clock of the blanking history (a debounce), instead of reading the one value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, if cp_sync is high BLANK_CLKS clocks before pwm rises but drops in any later clock before turn-on, the cycle is not counted, so fault_count_ss_out stays lower and window_trip_SS asserts late or not at all.

mutants.description: The soft-start window is sampled at high-side turn-off (the falling edge of pwm_sync, the peak) while the run window keeps using the valley at pwm_rise.
mutants.reason: In S_SS the sample reads the comparator from BLANK_CLKS clocks before PWM falls (during high-side conduction), so a comparator that is high only near the peak, or only at the valley, gives a different fault_count_ss_out and window_trip_SS than valley sampling does.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip compares count and threshold as signed values, so a trip_ss of 32 or more (top bit set) is read as a negative threshold.
mutants.reason: With trip_ss = 32 (a full-window threshold), window_trip_SS asserts as soon as S_SS is entered with zero faulted cycles, because 0 >= -32 is true.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip line is copied from the run-trip line and widens the soft-start count from the run-count width (FCNT_RUN_W), so a full 32-cycle soft-start count loses its top bit and reads as 0.
mutants.reason: When trip_ss is 32 (the highest value reg_file allows), a completely faulted soft-start window gives a count of 32 that compares as 0, so window_trip_SS never asserts. With a lower trip_ss, window_trip_SS drops again when the count reaches 32.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip is checked only on the cycle-boundary strobe pwm_rise, as if it were sampled together with the window, instead of following the soft-start count all the time.
mutants.reason: In S_SS with the count at or above trip_ss, window_trip_SS pulses for one clock at each PWM rising edge instead of staying high. It also reacts at the next edge, not at once, when trip_ss is lowered.

mutants.description: The soft-start window is rewritten to put the new sample in at the MSB and shift right, but the count still subtracts bit WINDOW_SS-1 as the leaving bit, and that bit is now the newest sample.
mutants.reason: In S_SS each faulted cycle is taken off again on the next pwm_rise, so fault_count_ss never builds above about 1 under a sustained overcurrent. window_trip_SS never fires for trip_ss >= 2, and the soft-start telemetry is wrong.

mutants.description: The idle clear resets the two shift registers but leaves both counts holding their values from before the hiccup.
mutants.reason: After a window trip and hiccup, the run count keeps its old value, for example trip_run. Because the cleared window has no faulted bits left to take off, window_trip asserts as soon as S_RUN is entered again. In the same way, the soft-start count makes window_trip_SS fire on re-entry to S_SS, and both telemetry counts stay non-zero in idle.

mutants.description: The sample entering the soft-start window is copied across the count width instead of zero-extended, so a faulted cycle entering the window adds all-ones (-1) to fault_count_ss instead of +1.
mutants.reason: In S_SS a faulted cycle makes fault_count_ss go down, wrapping below zero to large values. window_trip_SS then asserts on the first faulted cycle when the count wraps to 63 from 0, and fault_count_ss_out reports nonsense.

mutants.description: The new run-window sample is copied across the whole run shift register instead of being zero-extended into bit 0, so one faulted cycle marks every slot of the run window as faulted.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a single faulted cycle followed by clean cycles fills the window with ones, so fault_count_run goes down by one for each of the next 16 cycles even though it was only raised once. The count wraps and goes wrong, which changes fault_count_run_out and window_trip.

mutants.description: Both windows tap the blanking history at the newest end (cp_delay[0], one clock back) instead of the oldest bit cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1], so there is in effect no blanking.
mutants.reason: In S_SS or S_RUN, when cp_sync is high only in the clock just before pwm_rise (during high-side turn-on), or high 5 clocks before and low just before, the cycle is logged the opposite way, so fault_count_run_out / fault_count_ss_out and the trips change.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window is sampled at high-side turn-off (the falling edge of pwm_sync, the peak), while the soft-start window keeps using the valley at pwm_rise.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN the run window takes the blanked comparator value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before the PWM falling edge instead of before the rising edge, so a CP pulse during the low-side period near the valley but not near the turn-off is counted wrongly in fault_count_run_out and window_trip.

mutants.description: The soft-start window records the start of an overcurrent excursion (a faulted cycle after a clear one) instead of the comparator level, so a sustained fault in S_SS is logged only on every other cycle.
mutants.reason: With cp_sync held high through S_SS, fault_count_ss_out rises at half the rate, and window_trip_SS asserts later or never (for trip_ss above 16).

mutants.description: The soft-start window takes as its sample 'cp_sync high in any of the last BLANK_CLKS clocks' instead of the one comparator value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, a CP pulse in the last few clocks before pwm_rise (inside the blanking interval) counts as a faulted cycle, so fault_count_ss_out is too high and window_trip_SS can assert early.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window counts a cycle as faulted only if the comparator was high on every clock of the blanking history (a debounce), instead of the one value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a cycle where cp_sync was high BLANK_CLKS clocks before pwm_rise but dropped in between is not counted, so fault_count_run_out is low and window_trip is missed.

mutants.description: An overflow guard stops the run count adding the entering sample once it reaches WINDOW_RUN, but the leaving bit is still subtracted, so a full window followed by another faulted cycle drops the count to 15.
mutants.reason: After more than 16 consecutive faulted cycles in S_RUN, fault_count_run_out reads 15 instead of 16 (and window_trip drops for trip_run=16); when the faults then clear the count wraps below zero to 31.

mutants.description: The soft-start count's overflow guard is compared with the run-window depth (WINDOW_RUN, 16) instead of WINDOW_SS, so the count stops adding entering samples at 16 while still subtracting leaving ones.
mutants.reason: With more than 16 faulted cycles in S_SS, fault_count_ss_out stops at 16 (then drifts lower), so window_trip_SS never asserts for a trip_ss above 16, and the count wraps when the faults leave the window.

mutants.description: The soft-start window stops sampling once its count reaches a full window (saturation applied to the whole update), so a fully faulted window is frozen instead of rolling.
mutants.reason: After 32 consecutive faulted cycles in S_SS, later clear cycles no longer reduce the count: fault_count_ss_out stays at 32 and window_trip_SS stays high for the rest of soft start.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip compares count and threshold as signed values, so a trip_run of 32 or more (top bit set) is read as a negative threshold.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with trip_run set to 32..63 (meant as 'never trip'), window_trip asserts at once with no faulted cycles.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window stops sampling once its count reaches a full window (saturation applied to the whole run update), so a fully faulted run window is frozen instead of rolling.
mutants.reason: With trip_run set above WINDOW_RUN (no trip), 16 faulted cycles in S_RUN followed by clear cycles leave fault_count_run_out stuck at 16 instead of falling. Lowering trip_run during the run then asserts window_trip on a history that has already cleared.

mutants.description: An overflow guard at the soft-start depth stops fault_count_ss from adding the entering sample once it reaches WINDOW_SS, but the leaving bit is still subtracted, so a full 32-cycle window followed by another faulted cycle drops the count to 31.
mutants.reason: In S_SS with a sustained overcurrent of 33 or more cycles, fault_count_ss_out falls from 32 to 31 although the window is still fully faulted. With trip_ss = 32, window_trip_SS then deasserts.

mutants.description: The PWM edge detector's delayed copy pwm_sync_d is cleared along with the windows and cp_delay while neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active, so entering S_SS while pwm_sync is already high produces a false cycle-boundary strobe.
mutants.reason: pwm_sync (Osc_sync) keeps toggling while the converter is idle. If S_SS is entered while it is high, pwm_rise fires on the first active clock and an extra (clear) sample goes into the soft-start window, which puts the window one cycle out of step. A faulted cycle then leaves the window one switching cycle early, so fault_count_ss_out and window_trip_SS fall one cycle sooner than they should.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window is written as a rotate instead of a shift, so the oldest sample leaving at bit WINDOW_RUN-1 comes back into bit 0 while the count still subtracts it.
mutants.reason: After a single faulted cycle in S_RUN, the faulted bit keeps going round the window, and the count loses one each time the bit passes the top. 16 cycles later fault_count_run_out is 0, and 16 cycles after that it wraps to 31, so window_trip goes high with no overcurrent present.

mutants.description: Copy-paste slip: the S_RUN count takes its leaving bit from the soft-start shift register, which is frozen during S_RUN, instead of from the run shift register.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN the subtracted bit is a constant from the soft-start history. If that bit is 0, faulted cycles are never taken off fault_count_run_out and the count builds up until window_trip asserts. If it is 1, the count drops on every cycle, wraps, and trips at once.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window stops sampling once window_trip has fired, so the count is held as evidence at the trip value instead of continuing to roll.
mutants.reason: Suppose the run count reaches trip_run while run_active stays high. fault_count_run_out then stays at that value and window_trip stays asserted, even after the overcurrent clears and the faulted cycles should have left the 16-cycle window.

mutants.description: Copy-paste slip: the soft-start count takes its leaving bit from the run shift register, which is held clear during S_SS, instead of from the oldest bit of the soft-start window.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, faulted cycles that leave the 32-cycle window are never subtracted. Once a faulted cycle is more than 32 cycles old, fault_count_ss_out stays too high and window_trip_SS can assert even though the trailing window holds fewer than trip_ss faulted cycles.

mutants.description: While neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active, the blanking history is preloaded with the current comparator level instead of being cleared, so a CP flag that is high in idle or hiccup carries into the new attempt.
mutants.reason: Suppose cp_sync is high when the supervisor enters S_SS, for example after reset because the synchroniser resets high, or because the overcurrent persisted through hiccup. A pwm_rise within BLANK_CLKS clocks of entry then samples a faulted cycle that was never seen while switching, and fault_count_ss_out and window_trip_SS change.

mutants.description: The windows and counts are cleared when a window trip fires instead of whenever neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active.
mutants.reason: If S_RUN or S_SS is left without an overcurrent trip (g_en low, UVLO, OTP), the counts stay nonzero on fault_count_run_out and fault_count_ss_out through S_OFF, and the next soft start begins with the old history. On a trip, the counts are cleared one clock after it fires while the state is still active.

mutants.description: The current-protection flag is treated as active-low when it enters the blanking history, so a cycle with the comparator low is counted as faulted.
mutants.reason: While switching with CP_trig low, every switching cycle is logged as faulted, so the counts climb and window_trip_SS or window_trip fires. A real overcurrent (CP high) is logged as a clean cycle.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip also fires when the soft-start count, which is held through S_RUN only for telemetry, is at or above trip_ss.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with no run-window faults, suppose the held fault_count_ss is at or above trip_ss: it reached the threshold on the edge the FSM left S_SS, or TRIP_SS was lowered during S_RUN. window_trip then asserts and sends the supervisor to hiccup.

mutants.description: The run-count telemetry output reports the count of the present state, so outside S_RUN it shows the soft-start count instead of the run window's count.
mutants.reason: During S_SS, after faulted cycles have been sampled, fault_count_run_out shows the (truncated) soft-start count instead of 0, because the run window is held clear in S_SS.

mutants.description: The comparator flag is masked by 'PWM low' as it enters the blanking history, on the belief that CP is only valid in low-side conduction, so clocks taken while PWM was high are recorded as not faulted.
mutants.reason: If the PWM low time is shorter than BLANK_CLKS clocks (high duty), the tap read at pwm_rise falls in the previous high period. A cp_sync that was high there is counted as a faulted cycle by the original but as clear by the mutant, so fault_count_run_out/fault_count_ss_out and window_trip/window_trip_SS differ.

mutants.description: The soft-start window is written as a rotate instead of a shift, so the oldest sample leaving at bit WINDOW_SS-1 comes back into bit 0 while fault_count_ss still subtracts it.
mutants.reason: In an S_SS longer than 32 cycles that contains a faulted cycle followed by clear ones, the faulted bit goes round the window again and is subtracted a second time. fault_count_ss_out then wraps below zero to a large value, and window_trip_SS asserts when it should not.

mutants.description: The soft-start window stops sampling once window_trip_SS has fired, so its count is held at the trip value as evidence instead of continuing to roll.
mutants.reason: If ss_active stays high after window_trip_SS asserts and later cycles are clear, the original count falls as faulted samples leave and window_trip_SS drops. The mutant freezes fault_count_ss_out at the trip value and keeps window_trip_SS high.

mutants.description: The asynchronous reset clears the two shift registers but leaves both fault counts alone, relying on the idle clear to zero them after reset is released.
mutants.reason: If rst_n is asserted while the converter is running with faulted cycles counted, fault_count_run_out and fault_count_ss_out keep showing the old counts for the whole reset, where they should read 0. They stay that way until the first clock after release, and at power-up they start undefined.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window trip is also qualified by the live comparator flag ('overcurrent still present'), so a run window that holds trip_run faulted cycles does not trip while cp_sync is low.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, once fault_count_run reaches trip_run, window_trip should assert and stay high. With this fault it is held low whenever cp_sync is low, so an intermittent overcurrent that fills the window trips late, or never trips if cp_sync is low whenever the count is at or above the threshold.

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip is masked on the cycle-boundary strobe clock, as if the run count were mid-update there, though the count is a register and is valid on that clock.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, once fault_count_run is at or above trip_run, window_trip drops to 0 for one clock on every pwm_rise. If the run count first reaches trip_run and the next valley falls on the same clock that S_RUN is entered or held, the trip is delayed by one clock.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window advances only on cycles whose blanked sample is faulted, so clean cycles never push older faulted cycles out of the run window.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, an intermittent overcurrent (for example one faulted cycle in four) makes fault_count_run_out keep climbing instead of settling near a quarter of the window. window_trip then asserts once the total reaches trip_run, which a true trailing 16-cycle window would never reach.

mutants.description: The soft-start window advances only on cycles whose blanked sample is faulted, so clean soft-start cycles never age faulted cycles out of the 32-cycle window.
mutants.reason: In S_SS with sparse overcurrent cycles, fault_count_ss_out grows with the total number of faulted cycles since entry instead of the number in the trailing 32. window_trip_SS asserts once that total reaches trip_ss.

mutants.description: Only the run shift register is qualified by the cycle-boundary strobe. The run count is updated on every clock in S_RUN, so one faulted switching cycle is counted once per clock instead of once per cycle.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, while the blanked comparator sample is high, fault_count_run_out goes up on every clock and wraps. window_trip asserts within a few clocks of the first faulted cycle instead of after trip_run faulted cycles.

mutants.description: Only the soft-start shift register is qualified by the cycle-boundary strobe. fault_count_ss is updated on every clock in S_SS, so one faulted cycle is counted once per clock.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, while the blanked comparator sample is high, fault_count_ss_out goes up on every clock. window_trip_SS asserts a few clocks after the first faulted cycle instead of after trip_ss faulted cycles.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip is masked on the cycle-boundary strobe clock, as if fault_count_ss were mid-update there, although the count is a register and is valid on that clock.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, when the soft-start count is at or above trip_ss (for example after trip_ss is lowered, or while the supervisor has not yet left S_SS), window_trip_SS drops low for one clock on every rising edge of pwm_sync instead of staying high.

mutants.description: The soft-start window trip is also qualified by the live comparator flag ('overcurrent still present'), so a soft-start window that holds trip_ss faulted cycles does not trip while cp_sync is low.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, after the window count reaches trip_ss on a valley sample, window_trip_SS stays low while cp_sync is low, for example once the comparator has released after high-side turn-on. It asserts only when the comparator is high again, instead of as soon as the count reaches trip_ss.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count is updated by 'entering XOR leaving' (the count changes only when the two bits differ) but always adds that change, forgetting the direction, so a faulted cycle leaving the run window increments fault_count_run instead of decrementing it.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, once a faulted cycle reaches bit WINDOW_RUN-1 and a clean sample enters on pwm_rise, fault_count_run_out goes up by one instead of down, and window_trip can assert after faulted cycles have already left the 16-cycle window.

mutants.description: The soft-start count is updated by 'entering XOR leaving' (the count changes only when the two bits differ) but always adds that change, so a faulted cycle leaving the 32-cycle window increments fault_count_ss instead of decrementing it.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, after more than 32 cycles, a faulted cycle that ages out while a clean cycle enters makes fault_count_ss_out rise instead of fall. window_trip_SS can then assert on overcurrent that has already left the soft-start window.

mutants.description: The leaving bit is subtracted only when the window is 'full', but fullness is tested on the fault count (count == WINDOW_SS) rather than on the number of samples taken, so faulted cycles that leave a partly faulted soft-start window are never removed from fault_count_ss.
mutants.reason: In a long S_SS with intermittent overcurrent (for example every other cycle for more than 32 cycles), fault_count_ss_out keeps growing as a running total past the true count in the window, which is at most 16. window_trip_SS then asserts once the total reaches trip_ss, even though the 32-cycle window never holds that many faulted cycles.

mutants.description: window_trip is written as an 'any window tripped' summary that also carries the soft-start trip, instead of reporting only the S_RUN window.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, when fault_count_ss reaches trip_ss, window_trip asserts together with window_trip_SS, although window_trip must stay low outside S_RUN. Downstream logic would then see a run-window overcurrent during soft start.

mutants.description: The blanking history is also cleared at high-side turn-off (falling edge of pwm_sync), so that it holds only low-side samples, instead of being cleared only while neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active.
mutants.reason: At a high duty cycle, where pwm_sync stays low for fewer than BLANK_CLKS clocks, the bit tapped at pwm_rise is the cleared 0 and not the comparator value from BLANK_CLKS clocks earlier. A cycle with CP high is then counted as clean, so fault_count_run_out and fault_count_ss_out stay at 0 and window_trip / window_trip_SS never assert.

mutants.description: The bit leaving the run window is copied across the whole count width instead of zero-extended, so a faulted cycle that leaves the 16-cycle run window adds one to fault_count_run instead of taking one off.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, once a faulted cycle reaches the end of the 16-cycle window and leaves, fault_count_run_out goes up instead of down. Overcurrent that has already aged out of the window can then hold window_trip high or make it trip.

mutants.description: The run window and count are also cleared on the clock after window_trip fires, as if the trip itself should start a clean window, instead of being cleared only when neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active.
mutants.reason: After the run count reaches trip_run in S_RUN, fault_count_run_out drops to 0 on the next clock without a pwm_rise, and window_trip falls while run_active is still high. In the correct design the count and the trip hold until the supervisor leaves S_RUN.

mutants.description: The blanking history cp_delay only advances in S_RUN and forgets S_SS, so through soft start it holds the zero left by the idle clear and every soft-start sample reads as not faulted.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, if cp_sync stays high over trip_ss switching cycles, fault_count_ss_out stays 0 and window_trip_SS never asserts. In the original design both rise.

mutants.description: The S_RUN shift register stores the live cp_sync at pwm_rise, while the run count adds the blanked cp_delay sample, so the bit later subtracted as leaving is not the bit that was added.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, take a cycle where the comparator was low BLANK_CLKS clocks before turn-on but is high at pwm_rise. WINDOW_RUN cycles later that cycle's bit leaves the window and is subtracted although it was never added, so fault_count_run_out wraps below zero and window_trip asserts falsely. The opposite case leaves counts stuck in the window.

mutants.description: The soft-start shift register stores the live cp_sync at pwm_rise, while fault_count_ss adds the blanked cp_delay sample, so the bit later subtracted as leaving is not the bit that was added.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, take a cycle where the blanked sample is clear and cp_sync is high at pwm_rise (or the reverse). When that cycle's bit leaves the 32-cycle window, fault_count_ss_out is decremented for a fault it never counted (or keeps a fault forever), so the count drifts and window_trip_SS asserts wrongly or too late.

mutants.description: The soft-start telemetry output is registered, so fault_count_ss_out shows fault_count_ss one clock late instead of the live count.
mutants.reason: On the clock after a pwm_rise in S_SS that changes the count, fault_count_ss_out still shows the old value. On the clock after the idle clear it still shows the pre-hiccup count instead of 0.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.description: The leaving bit of the S_RUN window is subtracted only when the window is 'full', and fullness is tested on the fault count (count == WINDOW_RUN) instead of the number of samples taken, so faulted cycles leaving a partly faulted run window are never removed from fault_count_run.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with intermittent overcurrent (for example one faulted cycle in four over more than 16 cycles), fault_count_run_out keeps rising past the number of faulted cycles in the last 16, and window_trip asserts once the faulted cycles since S_RUN was entered reach trip_run, even though the trailing 16-cycle window holds fewer.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count is updated as 'decrement on a faulted leaving sample, else increment on a faulted entering sample', so a cycle where a faulted sample leaves and a faulted one enters decrements the count instead of holding it.
mutants.reason: With trip_run set above 16 and a sustained overcurrent in S_RUN, the run window fills to 16, and from the 17th faulted cycle on fault_count_run_out falls by one per cycle instead of staying at 16. Any pattern where a faulted cycle enters while a faulted one leaves undercounts, so window_trip is late or missing.

mutants.description: The soft-start count is updated as 'increment on a faulted entering sample, else decrement on a faulted leaving sample', forgetting the case where a faulted sample enters while a faulted one leaves, so it increments instead of holding.
mutants.reason: With trip_ss above 32 and overcurrent sustained through more than 32 soft-start cycles, fault_count_ss_out climbs past 32 (33, 34, ...) instead of holding at 32, and window_trip_SS asserts when it reaches trip_ss although a 32-cycle window can never hold that many faulted cycles.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip compares fault_count_ss for equality with trip_ss instead of 'at or above' it.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, if trip_ss is lowered below the count the soft-start window already holds, window_trip_SS stays low (and the supervisor stays in S_SS) instead of asserting at once. It also drops again if the count steps past trip_ss.

mutants.description: window_trip_SS is written as an 'any overcurrent window tripped' summary that also carries the S_RUN trip, instead of reporting only the soft-start window.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, when the run window reaches trip_run, window_trip_SS asserts together with window_trip, although the converter is not in soft start and window_trip_SS must be low outside S_SS.

mutants.description: The blanking history cp_delay advances only in S_SS and forgets S_RUN, so through S_RUN it stays frozen at the comparator history from the end of soft start.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, every run-window sample reads the frozen bit cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1] left from the last S_SS clocks. An overcurrent that starts in S_RUN is never counted, so window_trip never asserts. If the comparator was high at the end of soft start, every run cycle counts as faulted.

mutants.description: The soft-start window and its count take the blanked comparator sample from BLANK_CLKS-1 clocks before high-side turn-on instead of BLANK_CLKS clocks before, so the soft-start lookback is one clock short while the run window keeps the full lookback.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, a comparator level that is high exactly BLANK_CLKS-1 clocks before pwm_rise but low BLANK_CLKS clocks before (or the reverse) is counted the opposite way. This changes fault_count_ss_out and when window_trip_SS asserts.

mutants.description: The soft-start telemetry output is copied from the run-count line and passes on only the run-count width (FCNT_RUN_W bits) of fault_count_ss, so a full 32-cycle soft-start count reads 0 on fault_count_ss_out.
mutants.reason: When all 32 soft-start cycles in the window are faulted (fault_count_ss = 32, which is possible if trip_ss is above 32 or before the trip ends S_SS), fault_count_ss_out reads 0 instead of 32. It keeps reading 0 through S_RUN while the count is held for telemetry. window_trip_SS does not change.

mutants.description: Only the S_RUN count is qualified by the cycle-boundary strobe. The run shift register shifts on every clock in S_RUN, so the window ages by clocks rather than by switching cycles, and the bit the count subtracts as leaving is not a sample that the count added.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with a switching period longer than 16 clocks, the bit at WINDOW_RUN-1 on a pwm_rise is the blanked comparator value from 16 clocks earlier, not the sample from 16 cycles earlier. fault_count_run and fault_count_run_out then drift from the real number of faulted cycles and can underflow, and window_trip fires or fails to fire because of that wrong count.

mutants.description: Only the soft-start count is qualified by the cycle-boundary strobe. The soft-start shift register shifts on every clock in S_SS, so the 32-bit window holds clocks rather than switching cycles, and the leaving bit fault_count_ss subtracts is not a sample that the count added.
mutants.reason: In S_SS with a switching period longer than 32 clocks and the comparator high for part of a cycle, the bit subtracted at pwm_rise is the blanked comparator value from 32 clocks earlier. fault_count_ss and fault_count_ss_out then drift from the real number of faulted cycles and can underflow, and window_trip_SS fires or fails to fire because of that wrong count.

mutants.description: The S_RUN window and its count both take the blanked comparator sample from BLANK_CLKS-1 clocks before high-side turn-on instead of BLANK_CLKS clocks before, so the run lookback is one clock short while soft start keeps the full lookback.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, if cp_sync changes exactly BLANK_CLKS clocks before a PWM rising edge, the run window records the wrong level for that cycle. fault_count_run_out and window_trip then change.

mutants.description: Parenthesis slip in the S_RUN window update: the new sample is ORed in before the shift, so it lands in bit 1. Each sample reaches the leaving bit WINDOW_RUN-1 one cycle early, and the run window spans 15 cycles instead of 16.
mutants.reason: With a sustained overcurrent in S_RUN, fault_count_run tops out at 15 instead of 16. A trip_run of 16 never asserts window_trip, and faulted cycles leave fault_count_run_out one cycle early.

mutants.description: Parenthesis slip in the soft-start window update: the new sample is ORed in before the shift, so it lands in bit 1 and leaves at bit WINDOW_SS-1 one cycle early. The soft-start window spans 31 cycles instead of 32.
mutants.reason: With a sustained overcurrent through S_SS, fault_count_ss tops out at 31 instead of 32. A trip_ss of 32 never asserts window_trip_SS, and fault_count_ss_out drops a faulted cycle one cycle early.

mutants.description: The asynchronous reset clears the two fault counts but not the two window shift registers. The designer relies on the idle clear to zero the windows after reset is released.
mutants.reason: If ss_active (or run_active) is high on the first clock after reset is released, the idle clear never runs. The first pwm_rise then subtracts an uninitialised leaving bit from the count, so fault_count_ss_out, fault_count_run_out and the trips are wrong from the first sample.

mutants.description: The PWM edge detector's delayed copy pwm_sync_d is updated only while the converter is switching (S_SS or S_RUN). Through idle and hiccup it holds the PWM level from the last switching clock.
mutants.reason: Suppose S_SS is entered while pwm_sync is already high and S_RUN was last left while it was low. The stale pwm_sync_d makes pwm_rise fire on the first S_SS clock, so the soft-start window takes a spurious sample and fault_count_ss_out and window_trip_SS change. In the opposite case a real rising edge on the entry clock is missed.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip is gated by a registered copy of ss_active (the state from the previous clock) instead of the live ss_active, so the gate stays open for one clock after S_SS is left.
mutants.reason: When S_SS is left, for a hiccup after a soft-start trip or for S_RUN with fault_count_ss at or above trip_ss, window_trip_SS stays high for one clock in the new state. The header forbids exactly this, because the soft-start count is frozen through S_RUN.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.description: The S_RUN trip is gated by a registered copy of run_active instead of the live run_active, so the gate opens one clock late and closes one clock late.
mutants.reason: After a run-window trip sends the FSM to hiccup, the run count takes one edge to clear, so window_trip stays high for the first hiccup clock. Also, a trip_run of 0 does not assert window_trip on the first clock of S_RUN.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.reason: Say run_active stays high after a trip, and then the run count falls below trip_run as clean cycles age faulted ones out, or trip_run is raised. window_trip should drop but stays asserted.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.description: The S_RUN threshold is captured on entry to S_RUN and held for the run, instead of trip_run being compared live.
mutants.reason: If trip_run changes while in S_RUN (for example it is lowered to or below the present run count), window_trip keeps using the value from before S_RUN was entered. It fails to assert, or asserts against the stale threshold.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.reason: While the module stays in S_SS after a trip, window_trip_SS should fall once fault_count_ss drops below trip_ss, either because faulted cycles roll out of the 32-cycle window or because trip_ss is raised. With this fault it stays high for the rest of S_SS.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.reason: If TRIP_SS is changed during S_SS, window_trip_SS keeps using the old value: lowering trip_ss to the present count or below does not trip, and raising it above the count does not release the trip, until S_SS is entered again.

mutants.reason: In S_SS, once fault_count_ss reaches trip_ss, window_trip_SS is high for one clock only and then drops, even though the window still holds trip_ss faulted cycles. On the next clock fault_count_ss_out reads 0 instead of the trip count, and through S_RUN it keeps reading 0 instead of the held soft-start count.

mutants.description: The comparator flag entering the blanking history is copied across the whole cp_delay register instead of being zero-extended into bit 0, so a high cp_sync reaches the tap cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1] on the next clock instead of BLANK_CLKS clocks later.

mutants.description: The blanking history is written as a rotate instead of a shift, so the oldest comparator bit at cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1] comes back into bit 0 instead of being dropped.
mutants.reason: Once cp_sync is high for one clock in S_SS or S_RUN, the set bit keeps going round cp_delay, so every later pwm_rise sample reads as faulted until the next idle clear. The fault counts climb to a full window and window_trip / window_trip_SS assert after a single brief comparator pulse.

mutants.reason: With TRIP_RUN programmed to 0 (trip at any count), window_trip now asserts throughout S_SS, where the run count sits at 0 and the run trip must be held low; in the original it can assert only in S_RUN.
